text:
The Devils have the best process of any team in this group. They take 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 57% at 5-on-5 alone, both lines with Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier take about 60% of the chances, and the Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes pair has outscored teams 22-11. They draw more penalties than they take, and the penalty kill allows fewer chances than most.

What they haven't had is steady goaltending, which is why they traded for Connor Hellebuyck from Winnipeg on Oct. 23. He arrived and won seven straight. Jake Allen has been the problem when he plays, with an .858 and 4.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. As a team, New Jersey has allowed nearly 10 more goals than its chances against predict.

Saturday was the extreme version: a 9-6 loss in St. Louis, the first time this season the Devils allowed seven. The Hockey News' Mike Fink called it "a grim reminder that the defense is the position they must fix." New Jersey Hockey Now has also asked whether the 5-on-5 dominance is slipping, though the full-season numbers still look strong. Timo Meier has been hot, and Evan Rodrigues has 8 points in 10 against 5.0 expected.

At 15-8-0 our playoff odds have them at 93%. What we'd watch: how many starts Hellebuyck gets, because the skaters are doing their job.
